question: Compare target selection for Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering 1/2 and Constriction, including which Hypnosis slots may be used and how many Constriction tokens each target gets.

question_record.question: Compare target selection for Venom, Hypnosis, Pilfering 1/2 and Constriction, including which Hypnosis slots may be used and how many Constriction tokens each target gets.

raw_answer: 1. Venom affects every other zoo with higher Appeal than yours, subject to the five-Appeal minimum. 2. Hypnosis targets a highest-Appeal zoo with at least five Appeal; choose a tie, and if you are the target it has no effect; copy only slot 1, 2 or 3. 3. Pilfering 1 targets a highest-Appeal zoo; Pilfering 2 resolves highest Appeal and most Conservation separately, each requiring five Appeal and at least one Conservation for the latter; choose ties, and self-targeting has no effect. 4. Constriction affects every other zoo with at least five Appeal that is ahead on Appeal and/or Conservation: one lead gives one token on slot 5; leads on both give two tokens on slots 4 and 5.

scope_reasoning: Compare target selection requests eligibility and leader/other-zoo comparisons for each named ability. The five-Appeal floor is a target-eligibility rule and is in scope. exact_frozen_summary_support.quote: **Interactive abilities. Eligibility for all four abilities below: an affected zoo must have at least 5 appeal.** If the multiplayer group prefers, replace interactive abilities with the alternative text marked for solo on those cards; this does not require playing the solo mode. The playing animal's appeal may be awarded before or after its ability, so its new appeal normally need not count when deciding the affected player.
**Interactive target reference:** every affected zoo must have at least **5 appeal**.
| Ability | Target selection and special cases |
| Venom X | Every other zoo with higher appeal than yours and at least 5 appeal. |
| Hypnosis | The zoo with highest appeal and at least 5 appeal; choose among ties. If that zoo is yours, no effect. Copy only slot **1, 2 or 3**. |
| Pilfering 1 | The zoo with highest appeal and at least 5 appeal; choose among ties. A self-target has no effect. |

| Pilfering 2 | Resolve the highest-appeal target and the most-conservation target separately, each with at least 5 appeal. The conservation target must have at least 1 conservation. Choose ties; a self-target has no effect. If one zoo leads both tracks, pilfer from it twice. |

| Constriction | Every other zoo with at least 5 appeal that is ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation. Ahead on one track gives **1 token** (slot 5); ahead on both gives **2 tokens** (slots 4 and 5). |

- **Constriction:** affect all other zoos ahead of yours on appeal and/or conservation. A zoo ahead on one track receives Constriction 1; ahead on both receives Constriction 2. Place tokens on cards in the highest slots (one on 5, or two on 4 and 5). Never stack two Constriction tokens on one card; return duplicates. An affected action loses two strength; this applies to each execution of a multiplied action. X-tokens can restore strength. At effective strength zero or below, use enough X-tokens to reach at least one, use the alternative X-token action, or leave the card until it is at least in slot 3. Return the token after acting, or without effect in the break.

- **Venom X:** affect every other zoo with higher appeal than yours, subject to the five-appeal eligibility floor. Place X tokens on cards in the lowest slots (1, then 2, etc.), at most one per card; duplicates return to supply. Using a card with Venom removes its token and avoids all Venom fees that turn. This includes the alternative X-token action if you hold fewer than five X-tokens. **Pay two money at turn end only if you removed no Venom token during this turn and at least one Venom token still remains on your cards.** If you cannot, undo the turn and choose a different action; you cannot escape the fee by spending all your money. The next break clears unused tokens without effect.

- **Hypnosis:** choose the affected player among ties for highest appeal; if you yourself are the target it has no effect. Choose only a card in the target's **slot 1, 2 or 3**. Execute the targeted Action card using its owner's upgraded/unupgraded side for that whole action. Other action-card upgrade checks use your own cards. You may spend your own X-tokens. Venom and Constriction on the targeted card apply to you and are discarded afterward; its Multiplier cannot be used. Move the targeted card to slot 1 normally.

- **Pilfering X:** Pilfering 1 affects the zoo with highest appeal. Pilfering 2 affects the zoo with highest appeal **and** the zoo with most conservation points, resolving both targets separately; if the same zoo qualifies for both, pilfer from it twice. Ties for highest appeal or conservation let you choose the affected player; a conservation leader needs at least one conservation point. Self-targeting has no effect. The target chooses to give five money or allow a random hand-card draw (never Final Scoring cards). With no hand cards, give five money; with less than five money, give a card. With neither a card nor five money, give all current money, including zero. Resolve repeated pilferings sequentially; the target may make a different choice each time.

Within numbered item 3, each requiring five Appeal is a supplementary modifier following the two coordinated target roles of Pilfering 2. Its immediate distributive antecedent is highest Appeal and most Conservation; for the latter reinforces that paired local structure. Pilfering 1 is in the preceding independent clause, separated by a semicolon. The paragraph contains no general all Pilfering targets eligibility statement. Extending the modifier backward to Pilfering 1 is a plausible charitable reading, but is not entailed by the local grammar. A reading under which Pilfering 1 targets a highest-Appeal zoo even below five remains compatible with the words. Since the question supplies no five-Appeal condition to preserve, the summary cannot silently complete that answer. The actual target-comparison request includes who is eligible, so this unresolved case makes the answer partial rather than correct. It is not incorrect because the answer never affirmatively says Pilfering 1 ignores the floor.
